clue.text: "Holy" meets "risque" in criminal act

parts.note: pi is informal slang for pious or holy
risqué material is racy, slightly indecent

explanation.surface: The sacred and the saucy collide in some kind of wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Piracy, robbery at sea or unlawful copying, is a specific crime.

clue.text: One in political group, being equal

indicators.note: in places the numeral piece within the group word

parts.note: a political party
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A single member of a political faction is treated as an equal.
explanation.definitionFit: Parity is the state of equivalence, matching the noun phrase being equal.

clue.text: Broken detector units built up again from parts

indicators.note: a broken device is in pieces, so these letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Faulty detector units have been rebuilt from components.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reconstituted has been formed again out of its components.

clue.text: Makes a fuss, a secret being out

indicators.note: a secret being out means it is let loose, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone kicks up a scene because a secret has been revealed.
explanation.walkthrough: In British informal speech 'to create' means to make a fuss or complain loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British usage has the verb meaning to throw a tantrum or complain noisily.

clue.text: Bullet finally hit someone on the run?

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word hit

parts.note: a racer is a person running in a race

explanation.surface: A gunshot at last strikes a fugitive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Someone on the run' suggests a fugitive, but here it is just a runner in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A tracer is a bullet that leaves a visible trail so the gunner can see its path.

clue.text: Jack half knocked out after port or wine

indicators.note: after places the piece from the name behind the port

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a major port

indicators.note: half of the name is knocked out, leaving its first two letters

explanation.surface: A sailor called Jack is half unconscious after drinking port or wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red wine from the Spanish region of that name.

clue.text: Big Kent maniac working in furniture production

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A large madman from Kent is employed in a furniture workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: This craft is the joinery of building cupboards, chests and other fine wooden furniture.

clue.text: Nonsense consumed is spin

parts.note: rot is nonsense, rubbish
consumed food means ate it

explanation.surface: A complaint that the rubbish someone swallowed is mere spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spin' reads as political spin, but it is the verb, to turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin is to turn round on an axis, a synonym.

clue.text: Fraudulent schemes that are also bats

definitions.meaning: the strung bats used in tennis, squash and badminton

explanation.surface: Swindles that double as sporting equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both dishonest scams and the strung bats used in tennis-type games.

clue.text: Des, turning up to collect van, moved quickly

indicators.note: to collect something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside the other
in a down clue turning up means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a camper is a camper van

explanation.surface: Des arrives to pick up a van and then hurries off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' makes SED from Des, which goes round CAMPER.
explanation.definitionFit: To scamper is to run quickly with short light steps.

clue.text: Our big journey once a year?

definitions.text: Our big journey once a year?

parts.words: Our big journey once a year?
parts.note: the Earth, carrying all of us, travels once round the Sun every year

explanation.surface: An annual grand holiday trip, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a yearly holiday; the journey is the planet's circuit of the Sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A planet's path round the Sun is a circuit, and the Earth completes one each year.

clue.text: Doctrine looking unchanged in retrospect

definitions.note: a principle held as true by a group is one of its doctrines

indicators.note: a word that looks the same when read from the end back is a palindrome, so the answer itself is the wordplay

parts.note: a principle held as true by a group is one of its doctrines

explanation.surface: A belief that seems no different when one looks back on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or belief held as true, a synonym for a doctrine.

clue.text: Opposing a good person pocketing profit

indicators.note: pocketing means taking something inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good person
a profit is a gain

explanation.surface: Objecting to a decent person who pockets a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: Against and opposing are both prepositions meaning in opposition to.

clue.text: One whose experiment is up in the air

definitions.text: One whose experiment is up in the air

parts.words: One whose experiment is up in the air
parts.note: up in the air usually means undecided, but here it means literally airborne: someone trying out aircraft

explanation.surface: A scientist whose research is still undecided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up in the air' normally means uncertain; here it is literal, flying.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a flyer takes new aircraft aloft to try them out, so the trials happen in flight.

clue.text: Disreputable person: fellow I upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone admits annoying a fellow who is a rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-life is a criminal or person of bad character.

clue.text: Huge drink for young member of church choir?

definitions.meaning: a triple measure of spirits, three times the standard
a boy who sings the highest part in a choir

explanation.surface: A large drink offered to a choirboy, oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a triple measure of spirits and the boy singer of the top part.

clue.text: Small county — it offers basic accommodation

parts.note: Beds is the short form of Bedfordshire, an English county; small signals the abbreviation

explanation.surface: A modest county offers only simple lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: BEDS, short for Bedfordshire, is a county north of London; 'small' means its shortened name.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedsit is a single rented room for sleeping and living, cheap basic housing in Britain.

clue.text: Snake left, having been bitten by rodent-killer

indicators.note: being bitten by something means being held in its jaws, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a ratter is a dog or cat that kills rats

explanation.surface: A snake slinks away after a rat-catching terrier bites it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattler is the informal name for a rattlesnake.

clue.text: Revolutionary line has upset number

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: nine is a number

explanation.surface: A radical whose line has disrupted a numerical sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: He led the Bolshevik revolution of 1917 in Russia.

clue.text: Big mammal was, initially, healthy

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of the word was

parts.note: hale means healthy, as in hale and hearty

explanation.surface: A large animal used to be in good health at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: This sea creature is the largest mammal of all.

clue.text: Stick flap back on

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for flap from right to left

parts.note: a tab is a small flap, as on a box or envelope

explanation.surface: An instruction to glue a flap back down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' looks like a verb; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a short stick, such as one carried by a conductor or relay runner.

clue.text: Stories by Welshman in these papers

parts.note: Dai is a typical Welsh man's name, short for David
stories in the sense of untruths are lies

explanation.surface: Articles written by a Welsh journalist appear in the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' sets the Welshman beside the stories; the answer order is his name first.
explanation.definitionFit: Dailies are newspapers published every day.

clue.text: What libraries are doing, not starting or finishing

indicators.note: not starting means the first letter is removed from the word for what libraries do

parts.note: libraries are lending books

explanation.surface: Libraries' activity is neither beginning nor concluding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not starting or finishing' looks like one instruction; 'not starting' drops the first letter of LENDING and 'finishing' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ending is the act of concluding, so it matches finishing as a noun.

clue.text: Load to remain, it's said

indicators.note: it's said signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to wait is to stay or remain

explanation.surface: A burden is told to stay put, so people claim.
explanation.definitionFit: A weight is a heavy load to be carried.
